title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers

target_networks.name: 15 released architectures from random init or pretrained (SmolLM2, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Gemma, ModernBERT, UltraBERT, Mamba-2, RWKV-7)
CIFAR-10 MLP/CNN/ViT and AG News classifiers

domain: science QA (ARC), text generation/reading comprehension, text classification, vision

headline_result.text: Given ten labeled ARC questions, frontier LLMs free to design the architecture all built sparse fact tables reaching up to 54.4% ARC test accuracy, above what they achieved writing Transformers (about 36%), yet far below a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-0.8B (82.1%).
headline_result.quote: When free to design, all three compile plain-text facts into a sparse table queried by a fixed procedure, reaching up to 54.4% test accuracy.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: two runs per generation/condition for most rows; gradient-descent baselines one seed

key_claims.claim: An LLM-designed model beats the most accurate released Transformer the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800x fewer parameters.
key_claims.quote: An LLM-designed model achieves higher test accuracy than the most accurate released Trans- former that the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800× fewer parame- ters.

key_claims.claim: Written two-layer Transformers score below plain BM25 search over the very text the LLM wrote (by 8.0 points on average for Opus 5.5), consistent with interference between dense keys.
key_claims.quote: The six written two-layer Transformers of Claude Opus 5.5 all score below BM25 over their own text, by 8.0 points on average.

key_claims.claim: Pretrained models fine-tuned on ARC remain far more accurate than any written model.
key_claims.quote: fine-tuned on ARC remain far more accurate, with Qwen3.5-0.8B at 82.1%, leaving a wide gap for WSP to narrow.

key_claims.claim: When editing pretrained checkpoints, strong ones stay within about a point, weak ones near chance gain up to about twelve points, and some are damaged (UltraBERT-380M 63.7% to about 33%).
key_claims.quote: Editing leaves strong bases near their unedited test accuracy, lifts weak ones, and in some cases damages the base.

key_claims.claim: MIT's released edited Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint scores within half a point of its unedited base on ARC, MMLU and MathBench.
key_claims.quote: The edited checkpoint that Takehi et al. (2026) released scores within half a point of its unedited base on ARC, MMLU and MathBench and slightly below it on SQuAD in our evaluation.

key_claims.claim: On raw CIFAR-10 pixels written networks reach only 21-28%, and the 96.1% with DINOv2 tokens comes from the pretrained encoder.
key_claims.quote: WSP as studied here therefore does not reach images and would need input units that an LLM can name without a pretrained encoder.

limitations_stated.text: Written models only recall stated facts; they do not chain facts, and ARC-Challenge stays near 38% while MMLU stays at chance.
limitations_stated.quote: None chains facts across steps or com- poses a long answer. ARC-Challenge accuracy stays near 38% while ARC-Easy reaches 63%

limitations_stated.text: The claim about Transformers applies only to current LLMs writing weights from random initialization without running on data.
limitations_stated.quote: Our finding that WSP does not need a Trans- former applies to how current LLMs write weights from random initialization without run- ning on data.

limitations_stated.text: Data do not separate a table chosen because it suits writing from one chosen because it is a familiar retrieval baseline.
limitations_stated.quote: so our data do not separate a structure chosen because it suits writing from one chosen because it is known.

notes_for_review: Large, well-controlled study of WSP from scratch: three writers, 15 released architectures, gradient-descent and fine-tuned baselines, a BM25-over-own-text control, test-overlap/deletion checks, and line-removal locality tests. Its central finding is that what LLMs 'write' into weights is essentially a hand-authored retrieval table, which works on elementary science recall but not on MMLU, multi-step reasoning or raw pixels. It also independently scores MIT's released edited Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint and finds no change on ARC/MMLU/MathBench. The 'code' link is stated on the title page; gradient-descent baselines use one seed.
